title: Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism

maps.tested: Two consecutive readings both rated Very Important with no crash-course substitute offered.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'ML/FT'. The governance question here is a role trap: the chief AML officer, not the CRO, is the actor who files reports and contacts regulators. Customer due diligence, correspondent banking risk, and the three stages of laundering are the definitional core.

vardeezReading: ORR-10: Very Important. ORR-11: Very Important.

selectors.name: Trap: AML/CFT officer versus CRO role
selectors.what: Governance role question: who files suspicious transaction reports and is the contact point for supervisors and FIUs (the chief AML/CFT officer, not the CRO as such, internal audit or the front office), and which responsibilities that officer may combine (CRO or chief compliance officer) and may not (business line, data protection, internal audit).

selectors.name: Customer due diligence, reliance on other banks
selectors.what: Customer acceptance, identification and verification: basic, simplified and enhanced due diligence (PEPs, senior management approval), beneficial owners, verification before onboarding, numbered accounts, and why funds from another bank's account or an introducer never remove the bank's own due diligence.

selectors.name: Correspondent banking risk
selectors.what: Risk-based treatment of correspondent banking relationships: not all carry the same level of risk, risk indicators, and the group-wide and cross-border rules around them (higher of home and host standards).

selectors.name: Three stages of money laundering
selectors.what: Placement (disguising the origin of funds, including smurfing), layering (varying amounts and patterns to make tracking hard) and integration or extraction (getting the money out for use); matching a described technique to its stage.

notSelected: ORR-11 b (the USAA case study: regulatory findings and lessons) carries only a bare Vardeez focus flag and no shape or Map point, and the parts of ORR-10 a and ORR-11 a beyond the officer's role and the three stages (risk assessment and transaction monitoring, STR and terrorist-screening rules, the four-component control framework, the fraud triangle) are deliberately left out.
